title: Creamy Tomato Tortellini
subtitle: cheese tortellini in a quick creamy tomato and Parmesan sauce: a 25-minute weeknight dinner
imageAlt: Cheese tortellini in a pink creamy tomato sauce with grated Parmesan in a white bowl on a navy napkin
servingsNote: dinner for one big eater + one hungry eater, plus 2 lunches

beforeYouStart.text: Start the pasta water first; the sauce takes the same time as the tortellini.

steps.title: Boil the water
steps.text: Bring a large pot of water to a boil and add the salt.

steps.title: Start the sauce
steps.text: Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium and cook the garlic 30 seconds. Add the marinara and Italian seasoning and simmer 5 minutes.

steps.title: Cook the tortellini
steps.text: Cook the tortellini for the time on the package (usually 7–9 minutes for refrigerated), until tender. Scoop out ½ cup of the pasta water, then drain.

steps.title: Finish the sauce
steps.text: Stir the cream, Parmesan and pepper into the sauce and bring just to a simmer.

steps.title: Toss
steps.text: Add the tortellini and toss gently, adding pasta water a splash at a time until the sauce is silky. Serve right away.

fixIt.fix: Loosen with the saved pasta water, a splash at a time.
The water boiled too hard. Keep it at a steady simmer once they're in.
The Parmesan went into a boiling sauce. Take it off the heat and stir in a splash of cream.

saleTip: Refrigerated tortellini is often 2 for $8 at No Frills, and freezes well in the pack for up to 2 months.
swap: Frozen cheese tortellini: same amount, cook 2–3 minutes longer.
leftovers: Reheat with a splash of milk or water; the pasta soaks up the sauce overnight.
doneness: Tortellini tender and floating, sauce coating the pasta.
source: Based on tested creamy tomato tortellini methods (Canadian Living, Olivieri): store-bought cheese tortellini in a marinara, cream and Parmesan sauce.
prepAhead: Best made fresh; it takes 25 minutes.
reheat: In a covered pan over medium-low with a splash of milk or water, stirring, or covered in the microwave 2 minutes, stirring halfway, until steaming hot.

basic.note: Marinara and Parmesan only, no cream.

stepNotes.3: Basic: no cream; stir in the Parmesan and pepper.

fancy.note: Browned mild Italian sausage stirred through, and extra Parmesan on top.

stepNotes.1: Fancy: first brown the sausage meat in the skillet over medium-high, breaking it up, 6–7 minutes until no pink remains (71°C / 160°F). Spoon off the fat, then add the butter and garlic.
stepNotes.4: Fancy: sprinkle the extra Parmesan over each bowl.

plating: A snowfall of Parmesan and black pepper on top.

why.1-4: A little cream rounds out jarred sauce so it tastes slow-cooked.
why.0-1: Salted water seasons the pasta itself, not just the sauce.

funFact: Legend says tortellini were shaped after Venus's navel, as glimpsed by an innkeeper in Bologna.

keeps.note: cream sauces and filled pasta go grainy and soft
